claims.claim: An analyst with few AI tools can replace an external consulting team's discovery phase in an afternoon.
claims.evidenceSource: WebSearch results (secondary). Best evidence is the HBS/BCG field experiment (758 consultants, Organization Science): about 25% faster, 12.5% higher quality on assigned tasks. Faster discovery figures found (up to 90%, under four weeks) are vendor or self-reported.
claims.supportingEvidence: Search summaries only; I did not fetch the primary paper. Nothing found supports 'replace a consulting team's discovery phase in an afternoon'. The AI-assisted groups were also less accurate on correctness.
claims.confidenceRationale: Strong literal claim, no primary evidence found; the best evidence shows modest gains.
claims.recommendedAction: Qualify: change to hedged wording such as 'can compress weeks of discovery into days' or 'can shortcut much of', or attribute to a named source. Do not publish as established fact.

claims.claim: A junior can gather real customer feedback before a committee even aligns on an agenda.
claims.confidenceRationale: Illustrative rhetorical claim, not a measurable fact.

claims.claim: AI can churn out a 40-page deck, business case, and risk framework in a few minutes.
claims.evidenceSource: No source retrieved. Plausible given current generative tools but not confirmed against a source.
claims.confidenceRationale: Specific figure (40 pages) and timing; plausible but unsourced. Policy G2 requires any stated number to have a source or be hedged.
claims.recommendedAction: Hedge: say 'a lengthy deck' or 'dozens of pages' or 'a first draft of a 40-page deck' and keep 'minutes' as illustration.

claims.claim: Both might claim massive productivity gains. Only one will deliver actual business value.
Office politics worked because proof was delayed, information sat in silos, and showing a better way needed a budget; AI is making proof, information access and testing dirt-cheap.
claims.confidenceRationale: Interpretive thesis about organisational dynamics; no checkable figures. Research I found says task-level efficiency gains do not automatically translate to organisational outcomes, so it is a contestable argument.
claims.recommendedAction: Acceptable as opinion; consider softening 'dirt-cheap' and 'impossible to defend' if asserted as certain.

claims.claim: Organisations house two distinct tribes: Truth Seekers and Political Players; political players have typically prospered quickly.
claims.confidenceRationale: Author's framework, presented as generalisation, not empirical.
claims.recommendedAction: Keep as the author's framing; avoid implying it is research-based.

claims.claim: The leaders who win this decade will be the ones secure enough to let evidence outrank authority.
Seniority no longer grants a monopoly when democratic access to information and hard data can counter intuition.
